newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse reports surge in Jan-Oct turnover.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse reports surge in Jan-Oct turnover.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Tuesday its 1996 turnover until October reached 1.912 billion dinars ($384 million).
This compares to the total 1995 turnover of 717.6 million dinars.
But not all the news were that good.

"The bourse turnover was firmly on an upward trend until July, but since then the trend has reversed and we face a constant decline in market activity," BSE general manager Pava Zecevic told a news conference.
Zecevic said monthly number of transactions remained more or less unchanged, but the value was falling.
The decline began after the central bank launched a 10 percent reserve requirement in September and than increased it to 15 percent earlier this month.

According to the bourse data, the share of the central bank short-term bonds had been falling since last summer when the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) extended maturity of bonds to 60 days and cut the interest rate to 60.7 percent.
The share of the NBY bonds in the total BSE turnover slid to 48 percent by the end of October from almost 70 percent earlier this year.
Zecevic could not explain changes in investor attitude. "They are abandoning an almost risk-free investment in favour of instruments attractive only for higher interest rates."

Referring to earlier plans announced by the bourse to introduce an A list of most actively traded paper, Zecevic said the bourse still did not have key information on the degree of companies' and banks' indebtedness.
Another plan to launch commodity trading in September also needed more time until enough commodity brokers were trained.
"So far we have dealt only with financial derivatives selling commodities. We want to develop real forward activity," she told Reuters.
